verifications.claim: SpaceX successfully launched 25 Starlink satellites aboard a Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Monday, April 6, 2026, at 7:50 p.m. PDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Monday, April 6: Starlink 17-35 ... Deploy 25 Starlink satellites into low-Earth orbit ... Falcon 9 ... Space Launch Complex 4E from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California ... Launch window: 4:03 to 8:03 p.m. PT Monday, April 6, 2026'; R2: 'Starlink Mission Falcon 9 SLC-4E, California Droneship April 6, 2026' (listed under completed missions)
verifications.reasoning: All key details match exactly (payload, rocket, site, date, within time window); R2 placement implies successful completion; exact minute not specified but within confirmed window.

verifications.claim: The launch followed a Sunday scrub.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions a Sunday scrub or prior scheduling/delay for Sunday.

verifications.claim: The Falcon 9 booster landed on the Of Course I Still Love You drone ship in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Booster landing: SpaceX drone ship, nicknamed "Of Course I Still Love You," in the Pacific Ocean'; R2: 'Droneship' for April 6 SLC-4E mission
verifications.reasoning: Exact drone ship name and location directly stated for the mission.

verifications.claim: The latest launch was from Space Launch Complex 4E, Vandenberg Space Force Base, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Rocket launch location: Space Launch Complex 4E from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California'; R2: 'SLC-4E, California'
verifications.reasoning: Exact launch site directly confirmed for the April 6 mission.

verifications.claim: The latest launch had a payload of 25 Starlink satellites.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Deploy 25 Starlink satellites into low-Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Exact payload number and type directly stated.

verifications.claim: The latest launch had a southerly trajectory.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Launches from Vandenberg heading straight south traverse open ocean all the way to the Antarctic'
verifications.reasoning: Reference describes general southerly trajectory for Vandenberg/SLC-4E launches, not specific to this mission.

verifications.claim: Additional Starlink missions are scheduled for April 9 and 11.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Thursday, April 9: Starlink 17-21' (supports April 9, no April 11); R2: Upcoming Starlink SLC-4E on April 10 (no April 9 or 11 Starlink; April 11 is NG-24)
verifications.reasoning: R3 supports April 9 Starlink but not 11; R2 lists neither (April 10 Starlink instead), creating contradictory schedule information across sources.

verifications.claim: As of April 6, 2026, SpaceX has an upcoming launch on April 8 called NG-24 Mission.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NG-24 Mission Falcon 9 SLC-40, Florida ... April 11, 2026' (not April 8)
verifications.reasoning: Reference lists NG-24 on April 11, not April 8, directly contradicting the date.

verifications.claim: As of April 6, 2026, SpaceX has an upcoming Starlink mission on April 9.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Thursday, April 9: Starlink 17-21' (supports); R2: Upcoming Starlink SLC-4E on April 10 (no April 9)
verifications.reasoning: R3 (updated April 6) supports April 9 Starlink; R2 lists April 10 instead, contradicting the exact date.

verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NG-24 Mission ... April 11, 2026' (not Starlink); R3: No April 11 Starlink listed
verifications.reasoning: Sources list schedules as of around April 6; April 11 is NG-24 (R2), not Starlink, directly contradicting the claim.
